subject: Request: brief retention exception for support debugging (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Audrey Klein <audrey.klein@nimbushealth.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent: Short retention hold for debugging a production failure

Hi Redwood team,

We saw an unusual slew of 500s on our integration yesterday tied to inference requests sent to your hosted endpoint. Our engineering team captured a small set of request/response pairs that would let us reproduce the issue if we could keep those records intact for a short period.

Request: would Redwood be able to suspend deletion of the attached sample payloads and the associated request traces for 72 hours (until 2027-09-17 15:00 EDT) for debugging only? We are prepared to sign an access attestation and accept any reasonable constraints you require (read-only export, no retention beyond the window, audit log entry).

I'm copying procurement to document this request and security to confirm scope.

Attachments: Nimbus_Support_Request_20270914.pdf (1 page), sample_payload.csv (3 rows)

Thanks,
Audrey Klein
Director, Integrations
Nimbus Health
---
Audrey.Klein@nimbushealth.com | +1 415-555-0108

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: Short retention hold for debugging a production failure

Vivek / Lauren — forwarding Nimbus' ask. They want a 72-hour hold on deletion for a narrow set of traces/payloads. Attached are their example files.

Key constraints we should evaluate:
- Is the data in our hosted logs or in customer-provided payload store? (I suspect the logs since they hit our endpoint)
- Do we have a documented one-off exception process for short holds (90% sure?)
- Legal / procurement approvals (Rishi) — we may need a simple SOW amendment or attestation.

Proposed quick answer to Nimbus: We can do a time-boxed hold for 72 hours with an audit log and explicit deletion confirmation, provided Security signs off and Legal approves the attestation text. Can we turn this around in ~6 hours?

Soojin Lee
AM — Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Short retention hold for debugging a production failure

Soojin — thanks for flagging. A few quick notes from infra/security side: 

1) Operationally we can mark the specific request traces as "preserve until 2027-09-17T22:00:00Z" in our retention layer (we already support time-bound holds for incident investigation).
2) We should require: (a) a written attestation from Nimbus limiting internal access and confirming they will not request exports other than the debug snapshot; (b) that any export is redacted for PHI and only contains identifiers necessary to reproduce; (c) access to the preserved artifacts is only allowed by RedWood engineers on the infra incident team (no broad CS exports).
3) Audit trail will be logged (who accessed, when, reason).

I can approve this from an operational perspective once Legal signs off on the attestation; no long-term policy change required. I also want to run a quick scan to ensure the sample isn't full of PHI before we keep it — if it is, we may need a scoped data transfer agreement.

Vivek
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Short retention hold for debugging a production failure

Team — quick legal/procurement note: procurement@nimbushealth.com copied earlier; we should avoid a new SOW for a 72-hour hold. Proposed path: we provide Nimbus with a short attestation template stating (1) the hold window, (2) that Redwood will perform the hold for investigation only, (3) we will provide deletion confirmation at the end of the window, and (4) Nimbus confirms no PHI in the sample or accepts liability for PHI. If Nimbus needs an export, we'll require a signed export request and a minimal export checklist.

I will draft the attestation text and post it to the ticket (and loop procurement if they want an internal PO). For now, we can approve the hold pending Nimbus' signed attestation and a quick internal PHI scan.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Klein <audrey.klein@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Short retention hold for debugging a production failure

Audrey — thank you for the quick report and for sending the samples. Per internal review we can do the following: 

- Redwood will place a scoped, time-boxed retention hold on the referenced artifacts until 2027-09-17T22:00:00Z.
- Access will be limited to named Redwood incident engineers and will be logged.
- At the end of the hold we will perform deletion and provide a deletion confirmation (signed PDF).
- Before we enable the hold we need a signed attestation from Nimbus that the attached samples do not contain PHI (or that Nimbus accepts responsibility for PHI). I've attached the attestation template and a short checklist we require.

Next steps for you: please sign and return the attestation (attached as Doc A). Once we have that, Vivek will mark the traces preserved and we will confirm via this thread.

If you need us to create an export for your engineers instead of a hold, we'll need a signed export request and a short scope; that'll take a bit longer because Legal needs to review the export checklist.

Thanks — we'll stand by for the signed attestation.

Best,
Soogin Lee
AM — Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Attestation_Template_Retention_Hold.docx (template), Deletion_Confirmation_Form.pdf (stub)
